title: Bind an invisible verified session to a player independently of alias
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md, docs/design/SWARM-BRIEF-v0.md, docs/design/RULES-SPEC-v1.md and the listed sourceRefs before editing. The imported Rules Spec v1 is the canonical engine contract; the earlier prototype/T01-T10 interfaces are baseline compatibility, not current gameplay rules. Do not restore approval votes, Repair/Sabotage buttons, Witness or five-node tracks. Preserve original IP and engine independence from Firebase/UI/Node. Edit only ownership; publish APIs only through explicitly owned package entrypoints, preserving baseline exports. Use original synthetic fixtures, scoped tests/lint/typecheck and npm run check. Do not commit, push, open PRs, spawn agents, provision/deploy services, access credentials or alter swarm budget. Implement the pure verified-session boundary from an injected trusted verifier. Temporary principal/session ID and session generation identify a player; repeated aliases and avatar changes never authenticate or merge identities. A copied room code/session hint/alias/avatar cannot claim another player. Validate verifier output into a detached canonical actor and reject malformed, expired or mismatched session results with fixed failures. Provider token verification belongs later to A069 and is G4-gated; this task uses synthetic trusted verifier results only. Do not add account profiles, login UI, JWT formats or credential persistence.
acceptance: Two participants with the same alias remain distinct verified actors and can use different configurable avatar keys.
Untrusted body actor IDs, copied aliases/room hints and a stale session generation cannot authorize another player.
Malformed verifier data and exceptions return fixed privacy-safe failures without tokens or raw claims.
Tests cover identity changes and session revalidation with no provider SDK, browser storage or network calls.
